title: Man fatally shot by police was 'solid kid'
article: As he prepares to bury his son tomorrow, Ken English stoically struggles with the 21- yearold's criminal path that ultimately left him dead at the hands of police.

Jeffrey Black was shot to death by a York Region officer in Markham late Monday night after he and two other men fled a break- in alarm in a stolen minivan, crashed into another van and ran to escape police.
Police said he was shot as he struggled with an officer who tried to arrest him. The province's Special Investigations Unit is probing Black's death.

"You wouldn't know it from his criminal record, but he was a good, solid kid who loved family," English, 42, said yesterday. "He just strayed down the wrong path." He said his son made bad decisions as a young teen, running with the wrong crowd, ending up in jail as a juvenile.

"I think my son believed that the worst that might happen to him would be that he ended up in jail. Actually in this case it could have been the best," English said softly as he stood in the foyer of his Ajax home.
"I hope it's a lesson to other kids," he said. "If anything should come from my tragedy, I hope it might change something for somebody.
"You do a minor crime and it could go bad. You may pay for it with your life."
"I'm sure my son's not the only one," he said. "I don't think there's a family out there who hasn't had issues with their kids. Mine, unfortunately, just took a very bad turn."
Black was one of three men who police say ran from officers answering a break- in alarm in a Markham industrial area shortly before midnight on Monday.
After crashing into a van, the trio jumped from the minivan and fled on foot. One man was captured immediately and another arrested an hour later.

Black ran north on Alden Rd., near Woodbine Ave. and Steeles Ave. E., where he became involved in a struggle with an officer behind a warehouse and was shot. He was dead on arrival at Scarborough Grace Hospital. The SIU has named one subject officer and six witness officers in the case.
"He loved life. He enjoyed every bit. But this . . . I just want to take care of my son right now," English said. "That's what's important to me."
